sections.heading: Printf_Log — UART logging on GT32U2086
sections.text:
This bare-metal example calls `printf` directly through the SDK's built-in
word-only formatter and `_write`. The application only includes `<stdio.h>`;
it does not need to configure or attach a UART explicitly.
Enable `CONFIG_NEON_MDF_DRIVER_UART=y`; there is no separate printf flag.
The first printf call initializes UART0 automatically.

UART0 defaults to **19200 baud, 8N1**. The FPGA uses a fixed **10 MHz** clock,
following the Test_VP policy. `NEON_PRINTF_FIXED_CLOCK_HZ` applies to both
startup/device code and the application. UART is enabled in `sdkconfig`.
Disabling it excludes both the UART backend and console; an application that
calls printf will then fail to link.

sections.heading: Build
sections.text:
```sh
cd examples/Printf_Log
cmake --preset GT32U2086
cmake --build --preset GT32U2086
```

Outputs:

- `build/GT32U2086/printf_log`: ELF for the debugger or emulator.
- `build/GT32U2086/printf_log.bin`: raw payload.
- `build/GT32U2086/printf_log_image.bin`: 128-byte ROM v5 header and payload, programmed
  at `0x00020000` with the existing GT32U2086 tools.

Use the complete image for ROM boot. See [GT32U2086.md](../../guide/GT32U2086.md) for the
programming and XIP contract. This example does not add a separate GT32U2086 flashing
tool or bootloader.

Reconfigure for a board with a different clock:

```sh
# Board supplying a fixed 20 MHz clock:
cmake --preset GT32U2086 -DNEON_PRINTF_FIXED_CLOCK_HZ=20000000
# Or use the SDK's normal SystemInit policy:
cmake --preset GT32U2086 -DNEON_PRINTF_FIXED_CLOCK_HZ=0
```

Choose one clock configuration for the board and rebuild. The console defaults
to 19200 baud. The optional AttachUART API described in the guide allows a
different UART or baud rate.

sections.heading: View logs
sections.text:
Connect UART0 TX to USB-UART RX and share GND. Check routing and voltage against
the board map. Open the extension's Serial Monitor at 19200 baud or run:

```sh
python3 -m serial.tools.miniterm /dev/ttyUSB0 19200
```

Reset the board after opening the monitor. Expected output with the default
configuration:

```text
[INFO] NEON MDF printf ready
[INFO] printf via _write
[DEBUG] signed=-42 hex=0x1234ABCD text=hello
[INFO] counter=0
[INFO] counter=1
...
```

The counter uses a busy loop rather than a precise time interval. The example
stops in `halt()` if printf fails, including automatic UART initialization
failures; inspect the status in the debugger. INFO/DEBUG prefixes are strings
written by the application; there is no log-level filtering system yet.

For the API, supported formats and use in other applications, see
[PrintfLogging.md](../../guide/PrintfLogging.md).

sections.heading: QSPI_Flash_Read_Write
sections.text:
Standalone GT32U2086 firmware for indirect NOR erase, page program and byte verification.
The application starts at the `fpga:>>` UART terminal and waits for `r`.

sections.heading: Hardware and test region
sections.text:
Use a NOR connected to **GT32U2086 QSPI CS0** with IO0..IO3, SCK, CS#, compatible supply and
common ground. The bitstream must route these signals to the NOR. The automatic driver
route uses the package pins below; verify their connections on the board.

| Signal | GT32U2086 package pin |
|---|---:|
| SCK | 68 |
| CS0 | 72 |
| IO0 | 71 |
| IO1 | 70 |
| IO2 | 69 |
| IO3 | 64 |

Supported devices use the W25Q80DV-compatible command/status protocol: JEDEC
`EF 40 xx` or `C8 40 xx`, density `12h..18h`. Other IDs are rejected before array writes.
The NOR is external to GT32U2086 and can be soldered on the board. Its presence and routing
must be confirmed; a flash used for FPGA configuration may use a different connection.

**Reserve NOR offsets `0x0003C000..0x0003CFFF` exclusively for this example.**
Every write test erases this entire 4096-byte sector, including when testing only
128 bytes, and leaves the test data there. Original data is not backed up or restored.
Initialization and entering the menu do not erase/program the NOR array. Quad mode
can update status registers to enable QE while preserving the other status bits.
Protection/suspend causes write tests to stop; the example does not remove protection.

The offset is configurable in menuconfig. It must be 4 KiB aligned, after sector zero,
and inside the first 256 KiB; reserve the chosen sector outside existing images/data.
`Flash_Read_Write` is a separate example for internal GT32U2086 Flash.

sections.heading: Build and load
sections.text:
```sh
cd examples/QSPI_Flash_Read_Write
cmake --preset GT32U2086
cmake --build --preset GT32U2086
cmake -E env NEON_MDF_SERIAL_PORT=/dev/ttyUSB0 NEON_MDF_SERIAL_BAUD=19200 \
  NEON_MDF_UART_BYTE_GAP_MS=2 NEON_MDF_UART_LOG=full \
  cmake --build --preset GT32U2086 --target flash_uart_gt32u2086
```

Load `build/GT32U2086/gt32u2086_qspi_flash_read_write_image.bin`, which includes the 128-byte GT32U2086 header.
These apps execute from internal Flash and require the **normal** build profile.
CMake rejects `-DNEON_MDF_PROFILE=xip` because the app changes the QSPI configuration
and erases/programs the NOR. Booting/executing firmware from NOR is a separate test.
See [GT32U2086 build and boot](../../guide/GT32U2086.md) for UART-download and normal-boot straps.

Open UART0 at **19200 baud, 8N1**, local echo and flow control off. At `fpga:>>`, press
`r` without Enter to open the example menu. Enter prints a fresh prompt; CR, LF and
CRLF are supported. After stopping the run, press `r` at the prompt to start again.
No test executes automatically at boot. Send each command after the preceding result/menu.

sections.heading: Configuration
sections.text:
```sh
cmake --build --preset GT32U2086 --target menuconfig
cmake --preset GT32U2086
cmake --build --preset GT32U2086
```

- `CONFIG_GT32U2086_EXAMPLE_FIXED_CLOCK_HZ`: actual FPGA clock, default 10 MHz, maximum 60 MHz.
  Setting this value does not change the physical clock.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_FLASH_READ_WRITE_TEST_OFFSET`: reserved NOR sector, default `0x3C000`.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_FLASH_READ_WRITE_DIVIDER`: encoding 0..7 for `/2,/4,...,/256`, default 4 (`/32`).
  Test SCK is `SystemCoreClock / 2^(divider + 1)`; at 10 MHz, `/32` is 312500 Hz.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_FLASH_READ_WRITE_MODE_0` / `_MODE_3`: SDR clock mode.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_FLASH_READ_WRITE_TIMEOUT_POLLS`: QSPI FIFO/completion/abort polling budget.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_FLASH_READ_WRITE_READY_POLLS`: maximum status/WREN commands per NOR wait.
  Allow for the device's maximum erase/program time at the selected clock.

Polling budgets are not milliseconds. Wake/reset uses `/32`; command-only frames
use at least `/32` to make BUSY observable, then restore the selected data clock.
The driver owns clock/reset and pin setup. Application code accesses the NOR through
NEON QSPI APIs; memory-mapped loads are used only in `QSPI_XIP_Read`.

Normal array reads use **4-byte frames**, with a fresh command/address per frame.
Each frame drains one 32-bit RX word, waits for TC and BUSY=0, then advances the
NOR address by four. A 2048-byte verification therefore uses 512 read frames. Erase
verification also reads in 4-byte frames. Page programming uses up to 256 bytes.
The default CS setup/hold and inter-command timing fields are zero; there is no
software delay between RX words. This does not change the protocol's eight dummy
clocks for Dual/Quad reads.

Random-pattern Quad verification can still fail on the tested board, including with
four-byte frames. Use Single or Dual for the operating modes that passed the board
tests; Quad verification reports any data mismatches as FAIL.

Data buffers contain aligned `uint32_t` words, with the low byte first in serial/address
order. No DMA or peripheral interrupts are used. Abort returns the controller to
indirect mode and flushes FIFOs. A transport error ends the current run; an abort/cleanup
failure blocks future runs until FPGA reset. An incomplete transfer never reports PASS.

A successful build or software simulation does not establish physical NOR presence,
pin routing, signal timing or clock stability. Verify these on the FPGA/NOR hardware.

sections.heading: Menu
sections.text:
| Key | Operation |
|---|---|
| `i` | Print JEDEC ID, status registers, QE and capacity |
| `s` | Select Single: program `02h` 1-1-1, read `03h` 1-1-1 |
| `d` | Select Dual read: program `02h` 1-1-1, read `3Bh` 1-1-2 with 8 dummy clocks |
| `q` | Select Quad: enable QE if needed, program `32h` 1-1-4, read `6Bh` 1-1-4 with 8 dummy clocks |
| `0..4` | Generate xorshift32 data; erase, write and verify 128/256/512/1024/2048 bytes |
| `5..9` | Same sizes with fixed patterns |
| `w` | Repeat the selected write test; random tests advance the PRNG state |
| `r` | Read and compare the last successful program; no erase/program |
| `a` | Run all ten levels in the selected mode and print a sweep summary |
| `h` / `?` | Help |
| `x` / Ctrl+C | Cancel between complete operations; at the menu return to `fpga:>>` |

Here **`q` selects Quad**; use **`x` or Ctrl+C to exit**. Default mode is Single.
Dual mode writes Single because the supported flash protocol has no Dual Page Program.
Switching mode preserves the existing test data and expected buffer, so use `r` to
compare the same pattern through Single, Dual and Quad reads. Expected data is kept
in RAM and is invalidated on a new run/reset; use a write test before `r`.

Levels `0..4` use random data and levels `5..9` use fixed data at the same sizes.
Passing the fixed levels alone does not validate all data transitions. In Quad mode,
both programming and reading use four data lanes; changing the read frame size does
not change the page-program frame size.

Example sequence, waiting for each result:

```text
r   open the example from fpga:>>
s   Single
0   write/verify 128 random bytes
9   write/verify 2048 fixed-pattern bytes
d   Dual read
r   read the same 2048 bytes and verify
q   Quad
r   read the same 2048 bytes and verify
w   write/verify using Quad
```

sections.heading: Test flow and results
sections.text:
1. Generate the expected buffer in RAM. Random tests start from xorshift32 seed
   `0x6D2B79F5` and advance between tests. Fixed tests repeat zeroes, ones, alternating
   bits and mixed-byte words.
2. Check protection, set/confirm WEL, erase the reserved 4 KiB sector, poll WIP and
   read back **all 4096 bytes** to confirm `FF`.
3. Program pages of at most 256 bytes. Each page has its own WREN and WIP polling;
   no page boundary is crossed.
4. Read the selected byte count in 4-byte frames through QSPI RX FIFO into RAM and
   compare every byte.
5. Dump only the first 64 bytes and at most eight detailed mismatches. The summary
   still counts **every** mismatching byte in the selected range.

```text
[VERIFY] bytes=2048 mismatches=0 [PASS]
```

Controller TC means the frame finished; NOR WIP polling confirms erase/program finished.
Cancellation leaves the erased/programmed portion in place and reports an incomplete test.

sections.heading: QSPI_XIP_Read
sections.text:
Standalone GT32U2086 firmware that programs a known NOR pattern using indirect Quad commands,
then verifies it through the **memory-mapped AHB window**. The application itself executes
from internal Flash. Press `r` at the `fpga:>>` terminal to open its menu.

sections.heading: Hardware and test region
sections.text:
Use a NOR connected to **GT32U2086 QSPI CS0** with IO0..IO3, SCK, CS#, compatible supply and
common ground. The bitstream must route these signals to the NOR. The automatic driver
route uses the package pins below; verify their connections on the board.

| Signal | GT32U2086 package pin |
|---|---:|
| SCK | 68 |
| CS0 | 72 |
| IO0 | 71 |
| IO1 | 70 |
| IO2 | 69 |
| IO3 | 64 |

Supported devices use the W25Q80DV-compatible command/status protocol: JEDEC
`EF 40 xx` or `C8 40 xx`, density `12h..18h`. Other IDs are rejected before array writes.
The NOR is external to GT32U2086 and can be soldered on the board. Its presence and routing
must be confirmed; a flash used for FPGA configuration may use a different connection.

**Reserve NOR offsets `0x0003C000..0x0003CFFF` exclusively for this example.**
Every write test erases this entire 4096-byte sector, including when testing only
128 bytes, and leaves the test data there. Original data is not backed up or restored.
Initialization and entering the menu do not erase/program the NOR array. Quad mode
can update status registers to enable QE while preserving the other status bits.
Protection/suspend causes write tests to stop; the example does not remove protection.

The offset is configurable in menuconfig. It must be 4 KiB aligned, after sector zero,
and inside the first 256 KiB; reserve the chosen sector outside existing images/data.
`Flash_Read_Write` is a separate example for internal GT32U2086 Flash.

sections.heading: Configuration
sections.text:
```sh
cmake --build --preset GT32U2086 --target menuconfig
cmake --preset GT32U2086
cmake --build --preset GT32U2086
```

- `CONFIG_GT32U2086_EXAMPLE_FIXED_CLOCK_HZ`: actual FPGA clock, default 10 MHz, maximum 60 MHz.
  Setting this value does not change the physical clock.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_XIP_READ_TEST_OFFSET`: reserved NOR sector, default `0x3C000`.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_XIP_READ_DIVIDER`: encoding 0..7 for `/2,/4,...,/256`, default 4 (`/32`).
  Test SCK is `SystemCoreClock / 2^(divider + 1)`; at 10 MHz, `/32` is 312500 Hz.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_XIP_READ_MODE_0` / `_MODE_3`: SDR clock mode.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_XIP_READ_TIMEOUT_POLLS`: QSPI FIFO/completion/abort polling budget.
- `CONFIG_QSPI_XIP_READ_READY_POLLS`: maximum status/WREN commands per NOR wait.
  Allow for the device's maximum erase/program time at the selected clock.

Polling budgets are not milliseconds. Wake/reset uses `/32`; command-only frames
use at least `/32` to make BUSY observable, then restore the selected data clock.
The driver owns clock/reset and pin setup. Application code accesses the NOR through
NEON QSPI APIs; memory-mapped loads are used only in `QSPI_XIP_Read`.

Data buffers contain aligned `uint32_t` words, with the low byte first in serial/address
order. No DMA or peripheral interrupts are used. Abort returns the controller to
indirect mode and flushes FIFOs. A transport error ends the current run; an abort/cleanup
failure blocks future runs until FPGA reset. An incomplete transfer never reports PASS.

A successful build or software simulation does not establish physical NOR presence,
pin routing, signal timing or clock stability. Verify these on the FPGA/NOR hardware.

sections.heading: Menu
sections.text:
| Key | Operation |
|---|---|
| `i` | Print JEDEC ID, status registers, QE and capacity |
| `0..4` | Erase/program 128/256/512/1024/2048 xorshift32 bytes, then verify by mapped reads |
| `5..9` | Same sizes with fixed patterns |
| `w` | Repeat the selected write test |
| `r` | Capture and verify the last pattern once through XIP |
| `t` | Repeat fresh XIP captures, compare every byte and report CRC/good/bad counts |
| `a` | Run all ten write/verify levels |
| `+` | Increase SCK by decreasing divider encoding, down to `/2` |
| `-` | Decrease SCK by increasing divider encoding, up to `/256` |
| `h` / `?` | Help |
| `q` / Ctrl+C | Cancel between complete operations; at the menu return to `fpga:>>` |

`CONFIG_QSPI_XIP_READ_TRIES` sets the number of captures for `t`, default **100**.
Clock changes preserve the original expected buffer. SCK logs are calculated from the
configured input clock/divider, rather than measured. The initial divider returns to the
menuconfig value on a new run. Respect the NOR and board clock limits.

Example sequence:

```text
r   open the example from fpga:>>
9   program/verify 2048 fixed-pattern bytes
t   read and compare the same region 100 times
+   increase SCK
r   one mapped read with the same expected pattern
t   repeat at the new SCK
-   decrease SCK
q   return to fpga:>>
```

Use `0..9` or `w` before `r`/`t` in each session. Expected data is stored in RAM and is
lost on reset or a new run. A read test does not use its first capture as the reference:
every capture is compared against the **original programmed buffer**.

sections.heading: Test flow and results
sections.text:
Erase verification and page programming use indirect QSPI transfers with the same WEL,
WIP, page-boundary and protection checks as the read/write example. Quad Enable is
checked/enabled before the menu opens. The array is erased/programmed only on a write command.

Each mapped capture does the following:

1. Configure `EBh` **1-4-4 SDR**, 24-bit address, one alternate byte `FFh`, four dummy
   SCK periods, instruction sent on every frame.
2. Read aligned words from `QSPI_XIP_BASE + TEST_OFFSET`; the default address is
   **`0x3003C000`**. The GT32U2086 mapping window is 256 KiB, independently of NOR capacity.
3. Abort the mapped transfer to release CS, flush prefetch and return to indirect mode.
   The next capture creates a fresh mapping. Printing/verification uses the captured RAM.
4. Compare every selected byte with the original expected pattern. CRC-32/ISO-HDLC is
   printed as a summary; exact byte comparison determines PASS/FAIL.

```text
[XIP] bytes=2048 CRC=... expected=... mismatches=0 [PASS]
[REPEAT] good=100 bad=0 completed=100/100 [PASS]
```

The repeated test logs the first/last capture and at most eight failed-capture summaries,
plus up to eight byte differences from the first bad capture. All captures and all bytes
are still checked. Cancellation, mismatches or a transport error prevent an overall PASS.
The simple write/verify result dumps at most 64 sample bytes.

This tests the NOR **data-read mapping** and does not jump to a NOR application or
validate execution/boot from NOR. The normal internal-Flash build profile is required.

| FPGA pin | W5500 signal |
|---|---|
| PMOD_IO5 | SCK |
| PMOD_IO4 | MOSI |
| PMOD_IO1 | MISO |
| PMOD_IO0 | SCSn / CS |
| GND | GND |

with socket 0 closed and its TX buffer allocated; the power-on default allocation is sufficient.

Press `r` at `fpga:>>`. Each run does the following:

1. Configure mode 3, MSB first, hardware SS0, requested SCK 1 MHz and the driver default B2B
   pause of 10 SCK periods. Allow a conservative power-on wait of at least 560 ms.
2. Read `VERSIONR` using polling. Stop unless its low byte is `04`.
3. Write `00 01 ... 1F` using DMA TX, then read by polling and compare all 32 bytes.
4. Fill the receive buffer with `A5`, then read the same SRAM using DMA RX. A separate DMA TX
   channel sends dummy words to generate SCK. Compare all 32 received bytes with the pattern.
5. Release SPI0 and return to the prompt. Press `r` to repeat.

Example successful output, with iteration counts omitted:

```text
[W5500] VERSION=04 [PASS]
[DMA TX] Write 32 bytes to socket 0 TX SRAM: 00 01 ... 1F.
[DMA TX] Polling readback: 32/32 matched [PASS]
[DMA RX] Read 32 bytes; DMA TX sends dummy words to generate SCK.
[DMA RX] Compare: 32/32 matched [PASS]
[SPI DMA] TX and RX [PASS]
fpga:>>
```

Data mismatches report the first bad byte, its expected value and its received value. A failed
VERSION read stops before SRAM writes or DMA payload transfers.

sections.heading: Transfer flow
sections.text:
DMA0 channel 0 handles RAM-to-SPI0 TX; channel 1 handles SPI0 RX-to-RAM. Both use peripheral
request slot 1. SINGLE requests service one 32-bit FIFO word (four serial bytes), so each
32-byte payload occupies eight aligned `uint32_t` elements. RAM addresses increment; SPI
data-register addresses stay fixed. Peripheral burst ceilings are four bytes.

The CPU sends the three-byte W5500 VDM header with a 24-bit polling transfer. Payload transfers
use 32-bit words. CS stays LOW across header and payload. Receive capture is off for writes;
RX DMA is armed before TX for reads. The CPU polls completion and increments a work counter,
without moving payload words through the SPI data registers during DMA.

Completion requires DMAC done/idle with no outstanding bus transactions, plus the SPI DMA
completion flags. `neon_spi_wait_tx_complete()` also waits for TX FIFO empty and a conservative
final-frame guard before CS is released. A second guard allows CS release timing to finish.

SPI/DMA errors stop the current run. If a DMAC command has not retired, the example disables
SPI DMA requests, parks its two channels and retains the static buffers and SPI configuration.
It refuses another run until the FPGA is reset. Parking is not an acknowledged abort, so the
example does not reset DMA0 or reuse buffers after an incomplete command.

UART terminal. Press `r` again to repeat the example. While the run function is active, its own

`CONFIG_SPI_DMA_SCK_HZ` selects the requested SCK; the divider rounds the actual frequency down.
`CONFIG_SPI_DMA_TIMEOUT_POLLS` bounds SPI/DMA waits. B2B uses the SPI driver default.
A successful build or software simulation does not verify the physical DMA request routing,
MISO signal, CS timing or peripheral behavior; test the image on the FPGA and W5500.

sections.heading: Run
sections.text:
Press t to send 64 characters. Press r, wait for READY, then paste exactly 0123456789ABCDEF without Enter. q or Ctrl+C stops when a transfer is not active.

When the run function completes or its stop key is pressed, the application returns to its
UART terminal. Press `r` again to repeat the example. While the run function is active, its own
menu/data keys apply; `r` only starts a run when the application is at `fpga:>>`.
At this prompt, Enter starts a new line and prints `fpga:>>` again. CR, LF and CRLF are
supported; CRLF produces only one new prompt.
Configure with `cmake --build --preset GT32U2086 --target menuconfig`, then build again; changes to `sdkconfig` are applied automatically.
`CONFIG_GT32U2086_EXAMPLE_FIXED_CLOCK_HZ` must match the actual FPGA clock. Timeout values ending in
`_POLLS` are polling budgets, not milliseconds.

sections.heading: DMA configuration
sections.text:
Uses DMA0 channel 0, UART0 request slot 2, FIFO mode and separate TX/RX transfers. The main loop
polls completion and counts iterations. During RX, q/Ctrl+C are payload until all 16 characters
arrive or the poll budget expires. Compare TX output on the PC; RX compares with the fixed pattern.

The current implementation retains one character per `uint32_t` and a four-byte peripheral access.
This does not yet match the byte-oriented USART DMA profile in the DMA hardware specification;
hardware correctness and timeout recovery remain to be completed. Build success is not a hardware
validation of this profile.

sections.heading: FreeRTOS for GT32U2086
sections.text:
`FreeRTOS-Kernel/` is vendored from [FreeRTOS-Kernel](https://github.com/FreeRTOS/FreeRTOS-Kernel),
restricted to the kernel, public headers, GCC Cortex-M0 port and `heap_4`. Ports,
heaps and example projects outside the GT32U2086 scope have been removed. The root
and `portable/` CMake files are NEON-MDF build definitions for this subset. The
kernel retains GT32U2086 word-only patches for byte fields/access and static-object
layout assertions; preserve or port these patches when updating upstream sources.
The remaining kernel/port sources retain their upstream license; see
`FreeRTOS-Kernel/LICENSE.md`.

The `cmake/freertos.cmake` helper creates `freertos_config`, selects
`GCC_ARM_CM0`/`heap_4` and links the kernel with GT32U2086's word-only runtime
policy. Each application owns its `Inc/FreeRTOSConfig.h`. See the
[FreeRTOS guide](../../guide/FreeRTOSPort.md).

sections.heading: CMSIS for GT32U2086
sections.text:
`CMSIS_5/` contains CMSIS-Core files from [Arm CMSIS_5](https://github.com/ARM-software/CMSIS_5),
restricted to `core_cm0.h`, version/compiler headers and the upstream license.
Core headers outside the GT32U2086 scope have been removed. When updating the
vendor sources, keep Cortex-M0 dependency headers at the same version and verify the build.

`Device/GT32U2086/` contains headers, startup code and linker scripts generated
from `mcu-description/devices/GT32U2086.yaml`. The system files and
`gt32u2086_runtime.c` are handwritten. See the [SDK architecture](../../../../guide/Architecture.md).
